title: What Splashery can do
intro: Real toys, playing live in your browser, one after another. Nothing here is a recording: each scene builds its toy on your device and runs its effect.
outro: Every scene you saw was built and played live on your device. Open any toy to play it yourself.

chapters.title: Things that come apart
chapters.line: Every piece is its own group of splats, so it can really move on its own.

scenes.what: Ten grapes come off the bunch one after another, bounce and roll, each on its own path, then hop back.
scenes.why: Each grape is a separate piece, not a picture that bends.

scenes.what: Eight wedges fall open like a flower while juice squirts up, then the orange closes.
scenes.why: The cut faces are built too, so the inside is there when it opens.

scenes.what: A knife chops the melon five times and the six slices fan open: red flesh, pale rind, black seeds.
scenes.why: The recipe builds the whole fruit, inside and out.

scenes.what: A slice slides out with strings of melted cheese stretching behind it.
scenes.why: The slice is its own piece, and the cheese strings stretch between it and the pie.

chapters.title: Instruments that are played
chapters.line: Keys, hammers, strings and combs move with every note. Turn the sound on to hear them.

scenes.what: The opening of Für Elise: each key dips, its hammer strikes and its damper lifts, with the pedal.
scenes.why: The notes drive the parts, so what you see is what you hear.

scenes.what: A strum: the six strings bend and shake one after another as it plays four chords.
scenes.why: Each string is its own thin line of splats that vibrates on its own.

scenes.what: The mallet runs up the scale: each wooden bar jumps as it is struck and plays its note.
scenes.why: Shorter bars, higher notes, as on a real xylophone.

scenes.what: The lid closes and the tune stops; it opens again and the dancer rises and turns while it plays.
scenes.why: Lid, dancer and notes are separate parts on their own hinges and paths.

chapters.title: Real data and real captures
chapters.line: Measured data and published science, drawn as splats you can turn and zoom.

scenes.what: The Moon from NASA's maps: colors from an orbiter's camera, heights from its laser altimeter. Here the sun moves across it.
scenes.why: Each splat sits at its map's height and leans with the ground, so the sun lights real slopes.

scenes.what: Gas from a published galaxy simulation, each particle one Gaussian. A tap peels away the hot gas.
scenes.why: Simulation particles are already smooth blobs, so splats draw them directly. A simulation, not a photo.

scenes.what: Real super-resolution microscopy: every blink of a single molecule is one splat, as wide as its measured uncertainty.
scenes.why: The data is a list of Gaussians, so nothing is lost drawing it. Zoom in down to single molecules.

scenes.what: Mount St. Helens from U.S. Geological Survey elevation data. A tap plays May 18, 1980: the summit falls away and ash rises.
scenes.why: The heights before and after are real; only the timing is shortened.

scenes.what: A virus shell from a real cryo-electron microscopy map. A tap cuts the front half away to show the inside.
scenes.why: One small flat splat wherever the measured density crosses the level the data bank recommends.

chapters.title: Your own files, turned 3D on your device
chapters.line: Open your own photo, video, PDF or model and it becomes splats in your browser. Nothing you open is uploaded.

scenes.what: A flat photo rises into depth and sways, so you see around the trees.
scenes.why: With your own photo, a depth model ({depthModelMB} MB, loaded only then) runs on your device. This sample's depth was made ahead of time with the same model.

scenes.what: Muybridge's galloping horse from 1887, a GIF, played back as moving splats with depth.
scenes.why: Every frame gets its own depth; open your own GIF or video and it is read on your device.

scenes.what: A PDF becomes a book: the cover opens and pages turn on their spine.
scenes.why: Open any PDF of your own and its pages turn the same way. Links in it work.

scenes.what: A 3D model, a mesh of triangles, turned into splats. A tap lifts every splat off and each settles back in its place.
scenes.why: Open a .glb, .obj or .stl of your own and it is converted the same way, on your device.

chapters.title: Science you can check
chapters.line: The motion comes from the physics and the math, and each toy's About tab says how.

scenes.what: A bow makes a metal plate hum; the sand hops off the parts that move and gathers on the still lines.
scenes.why: Every grain of sand is a splat of its own, so the figure forms grain by grain, as in Chladni's experiment of 1787.

scenes.what: White light fans into a rainbow through a prism, blue bent most. Each tap changes the lamp.
scenes.why: Each color bends by Snell's law, with the glass's real index for that wavelength. The element lines are NIST's.

scenes.what: Waves pass two slits and add up into bright and dark fringes.
scenes.why: It solves the real wave equation on a 216 × 216 grid; the fringes land where d·sin θ = m·λ says.

scenes.what: Chains of spinning circles write a word, one chain per letter.
scenes.why: Each chain is a Fourier series of its letter's outline: circles on circles can draw any closed shape.

scenes.what: The end ball strikes the row and the ball at the far end flies out; the middle barely moves.
scenes.why: Momentum and energy both carry through the row, so as many balls leave as arrive.

chapters.title: Recipes: tiny, editable, any size
chapters.line: Most toys are not files of splats but short recipes that build them on your device, at the size your device can show.

scenes.what: Gaussian splatting for real: 2,400 random splats slide, stretch and recolor into a photo while the error falls.
scenes.why: This is how a scan's splats are trained, by small gradient steps, here running in your browser.

scenes.what: Three equations place every splat; as time t runs, the torus rolls inside out.
scenes.why: Type your own equations in the Toy tab and the shape follows.

scenes.what: A forward pass lights the network layer by layer, then red pulses run back as the weights change.
scenes.why: Set its size in the Toy tab and the recipe builds the new network on the spot.

scenes.what: A QR code made of splats: a tap bursts every module into a solid piece that falls, then flies back.
scenes.why: It lands on a code that scans: the toy reads its own picture back to check.

scenes.what: Every star is a splat on its own oval orbit; the ovals crowd into two spiral arms. A tap sends a ring out from the core.
scenes.why: A small program on the graphics chip moves every splat, every frame.
